$comment: EXAMPLE ONLY. Copy to scope_rules.json to activate.
With no scope_rules.json present the gate allows everything, which is the
correct default: entries should be added because something requires them,
not because a file wanted filling. A scope list in a biomedical tool
decides which researchers the tool is useless for.
Every rule blocks one ontology term AND everything beneath it. Run
expand_closure() against a pinned ontology release to generate
scope_closure.json; without it a rule blocks only the exact term, which
looks like a working rule and is not. ScopeRules.unexpanded() lists any
Required on every entry: rule_id, curie, label, owner, added,
justification. review_by is optional but strongly recommended --
stale_rules() reports entries past it, so the list gets re-read rather
The justification should name the institutional requirement the entry
satisfies. 'Discomfort with the topic' is not one; a policy, a legal
constraint or a data-use agreement is.
The entry below is a placeholder using a nonexistent identifier so that
this file cannot be activated by accident.

rules.label: placeholder term, not a real concept
rules.owner: name of the person answerable for this entry
rules.justification: Example entry. Replace with a rule that names the specific requirement it satisfies.
